description: Completeness ledger. Provenance proves emitted-code <= IR op (origin). This ledger proves COMPLETENESS: every claimed behavioral capability maps to the IR op(s) that implement it AND at least one conformance fixture that exercises it for real. AxAgent additionally carries a TypeScript-checker-derived public inventory: every constructor option, forward option, method, callback, event, observable, and public state member is classified. entries.summary: A real embedded engine executes model-authored code end-to-end through forward() and produces the completion -- NOT a ScriptedCodeRuntime returning canned payloads.
entries.state: VERIFIED IN ALL FIVE LANGUAGES: go (goja), rust (quickjs feature), cpp (quickjs profile -DAX_CONFORMANCE_QUICKJS), python (in-process quickjs wheel), java (quickjs4j/chicory via reflection). Each runs the full forward() loop through a real engine executing model-authored final() code, and an actor turn's console.log output reaches the next request's action log (agent-runtime-real-console-output). Engines are optional deps, so agent_runtime_real runs in engine-enabled build lanes, not the default conformance suite.

entries.summary: Across multiple distiller and executor turns, each turn's request carries the accumulated per-turn feedback -- the Action Log and the refreshed liveRuntimeState snapshot of live session variables -- so the model sees its own prior work and converges to final(), instead of re-exploring blindly until max_actor_steps. NOT a 1-2-turn canned case.
entries.gate: G1 real-engine antidote + G6 response perturbation
entries.state: VERIFIED via a real-engine fixture driving a 2-turn distiller and a 2-turn executor: the later request must contain a marker produced by executing the earlier turn. distillProbe7731 can only reach the distiller's 2nd request through the newly-provided distiller actionLog/liveRuntimeState (@build_distiller_inputs); the live state's 'distillProbe7731: ' line (TS's Live Runtime State lines, no 'Current runtime state:' prefix since 3a2 PR A) can only reach a request when @agent_runtime_refresh_state_summary repopulates runtime_session_state each non-error turn, and execLiveStateProbe8842 marks the executor's 2nd request. Proven to FAIL without the fix (distiller request was input/context-only and liveRuntimeState rendered empty) and anti-hardcoded by the response-perturbation gate (mutating the probe responses drops the markers and fails the runner).

entries.summary: Actor code can await the built-in llmQuery([{query, context}]) primitive: each item runs a focused sub-query through a dedicated AxGen (task:string, context:json -> answer:string) against the same client, and the answers return to the runtime as a real string[] the model indexes -- NOT a stub or canned value.
entries.gate: G1 real-engine antidote + G6 response perturbation
entries.state: VERIFIED IN ALL FIVE LANGUAGES via a real-engine fixture: the executor awaits llmQuery([{query:'llmQueryTaskProbe5521', context:{detail:'contextMarker8843'}}]) (both markers must appear in the sub-query request, proving the sub-gen ran with the passed task+context), captures the result, then finals with answer:'EXTRACTED_'+result[0]. 'EXTRACTED_subAnswerMarker9931' can only reach the responder request when the sub-query consumed the scripted answer AND the returned value is a JS array the model indexes with [0] -- which exposed and drove a Go fix (AxArray.MarshalJSON, so the wrapper struct serializes as a JSON array across the host-callable boundary) and an rquickjs fix (a host callable may claim an agent-declared reserved primitive name like llmQuery; only runtime-installed built-ins conflict). Each language registers llmQuery through a package-neutral seam (Go runtimeCallableRegistrar + goja RegisterHostCallable; Rust AxCodeRuntime::register_host_callable trait method + CoreHost::register_runtime_callable; Java AxCodeRuntime.HostCallable default method; C++ AxCodeRuntime::register_host_callable virtual recovered via code_runtime_registry; Python register_callable). Anti-hardcoded by the response-perturbation gate (mutating the sub-query answer or the executor code drops the marker and fails the runner).

entries.summary: When summarizerOptions is set, a pending checkpoint is summarized by a real model call (intrinsic.ai.complete_once) and the model's summary replaces the deterministic fallback -- NOT a canned value. Deterministic fallback is retained when the flag is off.
entries.state: VERIFIED IN ALL FIVE LANGUAGES. Uses the op-callable raw-chat intrinsic intrinsic.ai.complete_once (already bridged in all five incl. rust's scoped closure), so no new per-language host code. restore_runtime_state handling was added to all five agent_forward conformance runners to pre-set the pending checkpoint. The fixture asserts expected_exported_state_subset.checkpoint_state.summary == the model response AND summary_source==model, so mutating the model response fails the test (anti-hardcode verified: an impl that ignored the model output or hardcoded a summary would not pass).

entries.summary: The cross-run context map is read (injected into the distiller's context + the distiller prompt's hasContextMap section) AND evolved by a full TS-parity two-stage pipeline: a context-map distiller (itemTags + cacheCandidates) then a cartographer (ADD/DELETE/REPLACE operations), both via intrinsic.ai.complete_once. Operations apply to parsed [id] items across 6 fixed sections; helpful/harmful/stale tags adjust per-item scores; score-based eviction trims the map to maxChars; evolution is gated by infiniteEvolve || steps<evolveSteps. The evolved map persists through export/restore. Distiller scores AND cartographer operations are both asserted from the model, not canned.
entries.state: VERIFIED IN ALL FIVE LANGUAGES (full TS parity). Create: @agent_factory builds state.context_map from options.contextMap (map string/snapshot + maxChars/infiniteEvolve/evolveSteps/scores/next_id) -- agent-context-map-config uses a FRESH agent (no restore), the cartographer ADDs an item, and the exported text+scores+steps are asserted. Read: agent-context-map-read restores a non-evolving map (infiniteEvolve:false, evolveSteps:0) and asserts the map text reaches the DISTILLER request, isolating read from evolve. Evolve: agent-context-map-evolve asserts the distiller itemTags update scores AND the cartographer ADD operation mints a new [id] item in the rendered text (mutating either model response fails the test). Evict: agent-context-map-evict tags an item harmful and asserts it is dropped under a tight maxChars while the neutral item survives (flipping the tag to helpful fails the test). next_id is a persisted counter (no numeric id parsing -- rust mul rejects string operands, so ids are minted from the counter and eviction tie-breaks on text order). context_map is part of the export/restore state contract.

entries.summary: When contextPolicy.tombstoning is enabled, a resolved-error action-log entry (error turn followed by a success turn) gets its tombstone written by a real model call (intrinsic.ai.complete_once with the TS TOMBSTONE_SUMMARIZER_DESCRIPTION) -- a one-line [TOMBSTONE]: summary -- replacing the deterministic fallback, with tombstone_source=model. Also wires @agent_apply_context_management into the live forward loop (previously it ran only in the fixture op), so deterministic tombstones + error-pruning now run during forward().
entries.state: VERIFIED IN ALL FIVE LANGUAGES. agent-tombstone-llm restores an action_log with an error entry (tags:[error]) followed by a success entry, sets options.tombstoning:true, and asserts the exported action_log[0].tombstone == the model response with tombstone_source==model (the action-log sanitizer was extended to preserve tombstone_source). Mirrors the checkpoint summarizer pattern (llm_pending/llm_input set in @agent_apply_context_management, consumed by @agent_apply_llm_tombstone_summary post-loop).

entries.summary: Port-only (TS reads dependencies from a step's mapping function; the ports' execute(name, program) has none): a step added with a program and no reads or writes plans from the program's signature (intrinsic.program.signature, AxGen and AxAgent). It reads the input fields and writes {name}Result plus the output fields, listed as outputs. Output fields order later readers only (read-after-write), since a group runs from one snapshot and merges its results in step order; {name}Result keeps TS's full rule. A program without a signature (a nested flow, a custom program) is a barrier, as TS treats an unknown dependency. toString still draws edges from declared reads only.
entries.state: VERIFIED IN ALL FIVE LANGUAGES. entries.state: VERIFIED IN ALL FIVE LANGUAGES. derive-per-item maps an uppercase transform over ["ada","grace"] -> ["ADA","GRACE"] (per-item) and a scalar "lin" -> "LIN", with expected_request_count:0 (no model call). FIXES a prior gap where derive routed through stage_forward over the whole state instead of per-item (TS flow.ts:1321-1360).

entries.summary: AxFlow forward reads TS's cachingFunction (the call's, else the process-wide one; the flow constructor takes none) before it runs and before hosts open the flow's span and metrics: a hit returns the stored output and runs no node, a read error is ignored, and a run control skips it. After the run it stores the returned output, ignoring a write error. The call's function also reaches the flow's AxGen nodes. Keys are native SHA-256 digests of the flow plan and the sorted input values (@flow_cache_key); they differ from TS's keys, so a cache must not be shared across languages.
entries.state: VERIFIED IN ALL FIVE LANGUAGES against TS goldens (flow-cache-goldens.ts): the flow's and the AxGen nodes' cache reads and writes, the global fallback, key stability across input key order (reverse_input_keys), errors ignored, a node's read error failing the run, control skipping the cache, and a streamed hit. Each host reads the cache before the flow span, pinned by a host-side telemetry test per port. KNOWN MINOR GAPS (not ported, documented here): nodeExtended; multi-source abort-signal merge; finer step-level execution logging.

entries.summary: Generated provider transports decode SSE incrementally and expose a closeable target-native event stream through direct providers, provider routers, multi-service routers, and balancers. The decoder preserves UTF-8 across arbitrary byte boundaries, ignores only literal non-data fields, folds multiline data, accepts CRLF/CR/LF and an initial BOM, recognizes [DONE], and accepts a final complete event at EOF. Buffered custom transports remain valid. Retry and failover stop after delivery; cancellation and terminal states close the upstream response; usage and completion telemetry finalize only after full consumption.
entries.gate: test:axir verify plus generated provider_stream_no_key and stream_http_roundtrip examples (all targets)
entries.state: VERIFIED IN ALL FIVE LANGUAGES. Real HTTP examples flush a byte-split BOM/UTF-8/multiline/CRLF event, wait 300 ms, and prove the first event is observable before a final EOF-terminated event. Scripted seam examples prove [DONE], legacy buffering, explicit cancellation/upstream close, one usage event after full consumption, and a post-delivery upstream failure without replay.

entries.summary: A transient Anthropic error event is classified by error.type to its HTTP status (overloaded_error->529, api_error->500, rate_limit_error->429, client errors->4xx, authentication_error->auth, unknown->refusal) in both the non-streaming and streaming parsers. A pre-content streaming transient error (e.g. Anthropic's HTTP-200 overloaded_error SSE event) is retried with the same exponential backoff apiCall applies to a 529 before surfacing; the balancer then fails over on the surfaced retryable status (529 is in every balancer's retryable set). Generated provider, router, and balancer streams prefetch one event so retry and failover remain legal only before delivery; once a content event is exposed, later failures surface without replay or provider switching.
entries.state: VERIFIED IN ALL FIVE LANGUAGES via npm run test:axir. Anthropic error fixtures assert error.type -> error class + HTTP status (overloaded->Status 529, rate_limit->429, api->500, invalid_request->400, authentication->Auth, unknown->Refusal) on both chat and stream paths. anthropic-stream-retry-overloaded proves a first-delta overloaded_error is retried then the next response's content is returned; anthropic-stream-retry-exhausted proves the 529 surfaces once the retry budget is spent; anthropic-stream-error-overloaded opts out of retries (maxRetries:0) to assert the classification in isolation. balancer-status-529-failover and -stream-failover prove pre-content failover. Real flushed HTTP roundtrips prove incremental first-event delivery, and generated stream APIs close upstream responses on completion, error, DONE, or consumer cancellation.

entries.summary: A distiller respond(task, evidence) completion skips the executor stage entirely: @agent_forward re-types the payload to final and runs the responder directly (zero executor stage calls), guarded by directResponse!='off'. Executor prompts never see the direct-respond flags (stage-scoped flag clone). Executor-phase respond() aliases to final. Real engines install the respond global producing {type:'respond', args}.

entries.summary: A parallel group merges each step's changes, in step order, into the state so far (TS: the keys whose value is no longer the group's starting one). Every step in a group runs from the group's starting state, so merging whole returned states let a later step undo an earlier one's update. In the ports a program node's changes are {name}Result and every field it spreads (so a later step that writes a field's starting value back still wins), a derive step's its output field, a map step's {name}Result and the keys whose value it changed, any other step's the keys whose value differs from the start, and a step its guard skipped changes nothing. The result ends as running the steps one after another.
entries.state: VERIFIED IN ALL FIVE LANGUAGES. TS goldens: an earlier step's update to a key the input already held survives a later step in the group; each iteration of a while loop whose body is a parallel group keeps its updates, for program nodes and a derive step. Port-only fixtures: a spread field update survives, a field two steps spread ends with the later step's value, and it does so even when the later step writes the group's starting value back.
